questions.q: What is Vermont's state amphibian?
questions.explanation: The northern leopard frog got the nod in 1998, championed by Cornwall elementary schoolers.

questions.q: Vermont's state fish honors both cold and warm water. Which pair?
questions.explanation: The brook trout (cold water) and walleye (warm water) are Vermont's official state cold- and warm-water fish.

questions.q: The last confirmed Vermont catamount was shot in 1881 in which town — and the mounted cat is still on display in Montpelier?
questions.explanation: The 'Barnard panther,' shot by Alexander Crowell in 1881, is displayed at the Vermont History Museum — the state's last confirmed mountain lion.

questions.q: Why is fall foliage in Vermont so exceptionally red compared to Europe's autumn?
choices: It's a myth — the colors are the same
Sugar maples produce anthocyanins that turn scarlet in cold snaps
questions.explanation: Cool nights and sunny days trap sugars in maple leaves, producing red anthocyanin pigments — peak color usually hits early October.

questions.q: 'Stick season' is the Vermont term for what?
choices: The gray weeks between leaf-drop and first snow
questions.explanation: November's bare-branch limbo — made nationally famous by Vermont musician Noah Kahan's song 'Stick Season.'

questions.q: Noah Kahan, whose 2022 hit 'Stick Season' name-checks Vermont life, grew up in which town?
questions.explanation: Kahan was raised in Strafford, Vermont, and 'Stick Season' turned Vermont's bleakest month into a stadium singalong.

questions.q: What is Vermont's infamous 'fifth season'?
questions.explanation: When the frost lets go in March and April, dirt roads dissolve — mud season is the price of spring.

questions.q: Lake Champlain's spring flood record was smashed in 2011 when the lake crested at about what level?
questions.explanation: The lake hit a record ~103.2 feet in May 2011, flooding shoreline neighborhoods weeks before Irene hit the same year.

questions.q: Vermont sits in USDA plant hardiness zones that gardeners must respect. Burlington is roughly zone…
questions.explanation: The Champlain Valley sits around zone 5 (with recent maps nudging Burlington to 5b) — the NEK drops to a brutal zone 3–4.

questions.q: The 'Valentine's Day storm' Burlingtonians still talk about dropped over 25 inches of snow in which year?
questions.explanation: February 14, 2007 brought 25.7 inches — Burlington's second-biggest storm on record.

questions.q: What does Vermont spread on winter roads that turns cars into rust buckets?
questions.explanation: Salt keeps the roads clear and eats every Subaru's rocker panels — rustproofing is a Vermont ritual.

questions.q: Vermont's official state butterfly is what?
questions.explanation: The monarch became the state butterfly in 1987 — milkweed-filled Vermont hayfields are prime monarch habitat.

questions.q: Vermont's flag features the state coat of arms on a blue field. What tree stands at its center?
questions.explanation: The coat of arms shows a tall pine — a nod to the 'Green Mountain Boys' pine-bough badge — with a cow, sheaves of wheat, and a deer head crest.

questions.q: What is Vermont's state mineral?
questions.explanation: Talc, long mined in Vermont's ultramafic belt, was designated the state mineral in 1991.

questions.q: Vermont's state gem, found in Eden and once mined commercially there, is what?
questions.explanation: Grossular garnet from Eden Mills became the state gem in 1991.

questions.q: The first Green Up Day, when Vermonters clean every roadside in the state, was held in 1970 — a national first. When is it held each year?
questions.explanation: Governor Deane Davis launched Green Up Day in April 1970 (closing the interstates for it); it settled on the first Saturday in May.

questions.q: Vermont banned what roadside feature in 1968, one of only four states to do so?
questions.explanation: Vermont, Maine, Hawaii, and Alaska ban billboards; Vermont's 1968 law keeps the viewsheds clear.

questions.q: How does Burlington's sunset over Lake Champlain rank in local lore?
choices: The Adirondack backdrop makes it a nightly public event at the waterfront
questions.explanation: Because Burlington faces west over 10 miles of open water to the Adirondacks, its sunsets are the city's free nightly show.

questions.q: The average date of Burlington's first measurable snowfall lands in which month?
questions.explanation: Burlington typically sees its first accumulating snow in mid-November, though October dustings happen.

questions.q: 'The Champlain Islands are Vermont's banana belt' — why do locals say that?
choices: The lake keeps them warmer, with vineyards and long growing seasons
questions.explanation: Surrounded by the lake's moderating water, Grand Isle County enjoys Vermont's mildest climate — hence its vineyards and orchards.

questions.q: Vermont's state quarter (2001) shows a man doing what?
questions.explanation: The quarter depicts sugaring — sap buckets on maples — with Camel's Hump behind.

questions.q: Which poet, four-time Pulitzer winner, kept a summer writing cabin in Ripton and is buried in Bennington?
questions.explanation: Robert Frost farmed and wrote in Shaftsbury and Ripton for four decades and was Vermont's poet laureate.

questions.q: Robert Frost's epitaph in Old Bennington reads what?
choices: 'And miles to go before I sleep'
'I had a lover's quarrel with the world'
questions.explanation: The line comes from his poem 'The Lesson for Today.'

questions.q: Which British author wrote 'The Jungle Book' while living at his house 'Naulakha' near Brattleboro in the 1890s?
questions.explanation: Kipling built Naulakha in Dummerston, Vermont, married a Brattleboro woman, and wrote the Jungle Books and 'Captains Courageous' there.

questions.q: Jody Williams, the 1997 Nobel Peace Prize laureate who led the campaign to ban landmines, is a graduate of which Vermont university?
questions.explanation: The Vermont-raised activist earned her B.A. at UVM in 1972 before coordinating the International Campaign to Ban Landmines.

questions.q: Which 'Boogie Nights' and 'Poker Face' character actor has lived in Vermont since the 1990s and is a beloved Northeast Kingdom sighting?
questions.explanation: Luis Guzmán lives in Sutton, Vermont, and even ran (jokingly) for local office; he's famously generous around town.

questions.q: Tim Burton filmed the small-town scenes of which 1988 classic in East Corinth, Vermont?
questions.explanation: East Corinth played Winter River in 'Beetlejuice'; the production returned in 2023 to shoot the sequel there.

questions.q: The bumbling state troopers of 'Super Troopers' (2001) patrol the fictional Vermont town of…
questions.explanation: Broken Lizard's cult comedy is set in Spurbury, Vermont near the Canadian border — though most filming happened in New York.

questions.q: The Bob Newhart sitcom 'Newhart' (1982–90) was set at an inn in which state?
questions.explanation: The Stratford Inn's exterior shots used the real Waybury Inn in East Middlebury, Vermont — which still trades on the fame.

questions.q: 'White Christmas' (1954) climaxes at an inn in which fictional Vermont town?
questions.explanation: Bing Crosby and company save the general's inn in Pine Tree, Vermont — cementing the state's snowy-Christmas brand.

questions.q: In 2007, which Vermont town beat 13 rivals nationwide to host the premiere of 'The Simpsons Movie'?
questions.explanation: Springfield, Vermont won the 'which Springfield?' contest with a video of a giant pink donut, earning the movie's hometown premiere.

questions.q: Norman Rockwell painted his 'Four Freedoms' while living in which Vermont town, using neighbors as models?
questions.explanation: Rockwell lived in Arlington from 1939 to 1953; his Vermont neighbors posed for many Saturday Evening Post covers.

questions.q: Which beloved 'Everwood' and 'Deep Rising' actor, a longtime Dorset resident, died in a 2023 motorcycle crash that Vermont widely mourned?
questions.explanation: Treat Williams lived in Dorset for decades and was a fixture of Manchester-area life.

questions.q: Bill W., co-founder of Alcoholics Anonymous, was born in 1895 in which Vermont village?
questions.explanation: William Griffith Wilson was born behind the bar of his family's East Dorset inn; the Wilson House there is now a place of pilgrimage.

questions.q: Ida May Fuller of Ludlow, Vermont made history in 1940 by receiving the first what?
questions.explanation: Check 00-000-001, for $22.54, went to retired legal secretary Ida May Fuller — she lived to 100 and collected nearly $23,000.

questions.q: George Perkins Marsh of Woodstock is remembered as America's first great what?
questions.explanation: Marsh's 1864 'Man and Nature' founded the conservation movement; his boyhood farm is now Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park.

questions.q: Vermont's only national park unit, in Woodstock, is called what?
questions.explanation: The park preserves the Marsh farm and Billings/Rockefeller conservation legacy — the only National Park Service park in Vermont.

questions.q: Which Burlington-founded electric-aviation company is building the 'Alia' aircraft beside the airport?
questions.explanation: Beta Technologies, founded by Kyle Clark in 2017, builds electric aircraft in South Burlington and has flown Alia across the country.

questions.q: The huge Essex Junction chip fab, Vermont's industrial anchor since IBM built it in 1957, is now run by which company?
questions.explanation: GlobalFoundries took over IBM's microelectronics plant in 2015; it remains one of Vermont's largest private employers.

questions.q: Which 'green' household products company was co-founded in Burlington in 1988 and named for an Iroquois principle?
questions.explanation: Seventh Generation takes its name from the Haudenosaunee teaching to consider the seventh generation to come; Unilever bought it in 2016.

questions.q: Burlington tech success story Dealer.com, sold for about $1 billion in 2014, built software for what industry?
questions.explanation: Dealer.com grew to nearly 1,000 local employees making dealership websites, seeding much of Burlington's tech scene.

questions.q: The Vermont Teddy Bear Company, with its famous factory tours and 'Bear-Grams,' is based in which town?
questions.explanation: Vermont Teddy Bear's Shelburne factory tour is a Route 7 family staple.

questions.q: Orvis, the storied fly-fishing and outdoor brand founded in 1856, calls which Vermont town home?
questions.explanation: Charles F. Orvis founded the company in Manchester, where its flagship store and rod shop still operate.

questions.q: Crooner and 1920s megastar Rudy Vallée grew up partly in which remote Vermont railroad town?
questions.explanation: Vallée was born in Island Pond in 1901 before his family moved to Maine; the town still claims him.

questions.q: Stephen A. Douglas, who debated Lincoln in 1858, was born in which Vermont town?
questions.explanation: The 'Little Giant' was born in Brandon in 1813 and left Vermont at 20.

questions.q: Admiral George Dewey, 'the hero of Manila Bay,' hailed from which Vermont city?
questions.explanation: Dewey, born in Montpelier in 1837, remains the only person ever to hold the rank Admiral of the Navy.

questions.q: Which fiery abolitionist congressman, raised in Danville and Peacham, drove Reconstruction and was played by Tommy Lee Jones in 'Lincoln'?
questions.explanation: Thaddeus Stevens grew up poor in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom before becoming the House's radical Republican leader.

questions.q: Katherine Paterson, the Barre-based author and two-time Newbery medalist, wrote which classic?
questions.explanation: Paterson, a longtime Barre resident, wrote 'Bridge to Terabithia' and 'Jacob Have I Loved.'

questions.q: Novelist Chris Bohjalian, whose 'Midwives' was an Oprah's Book Club pick set in Vermont, lives in which small town?
questions.explanation: Bohjalian has written for decades from Lincoln, Vermont, and long penned a column about small-town life there.

questions.q: Archer Mayor's long-running detective series stars Joe Gunther, a cop based in which Vermont town?
questions.explanation: Mayor, a real-life death investigator, has set 30+ Joe Gunther police procedurals in and around Brattleboro.

questions.q: Howard Frank Mosher's novels like 'Where the Rivers Flow North' immortalized which Vermont region?
questions.explanation: Mosher wrote from Irasburg about the Kingdom's loggers, farmers, and outlaws; several books became Jay Craven films.

questions.q: Emma Willard, the pioneer of women's higher education, opened her first school for girls in 1814 in which Vermont town?
questions.explanation: Willard ran a female seminary from her Middlebury home after being barred from the town's college, before founding her famous Troy school.

questions.q: The Fairbanks Museum in St. Johnsbury houses Vermont's only public what?
questions.explanation: The 1889 natural-history museum's Lyman Spitzer Jr. Planetarium is the only public planetarium in the state.

questions.q: Which Vermont-born religious leader founded the Oneida Community after developing his 'perfectionist' theology in Putney?
questions.explanation: Noyes, born in Brattleboro, ran his first commune in Putney before decamping to Oneida, New York in 1848.

questions.q: William Miller, whose failed 1844 prediction of the Second Coming became 'the Great Disappointment,' spent his youth and formed his ideas around which Vermont town?
questions.explanation: Miller grew up and studied in Poultney before preaching from nearby Low Hampton, NY; Millerism became the root of Seventh-day Adventism.

questions.q: The founder of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was born on a hilltop farm in Sharon, Vermont in 1805. Who was he?
questions.explanation: A 38.5-foot granite obelisk — one foot for each year of his life — marks Joseph Smith's birthplace in Sharon.

questions.q: Which duo met in a seventh-grade gym class in Merrick, New York before founding Vermont's most famous food company?
questions.explanation: Ben and Jerry bonded as the two slowest kids running the track, then moved to Burlington to open their scoop shop.

questions.q: How many blocks of Church Street are closed to traffic as the Marketplace?
questions.explanation: The brick pedestrian mall runs four blocks, from Pearl Street down to Main Street.

questions.q: The twin granite 'whale tails' sculpture that startles I-89 drivers in South Burlington is officially titled what?
questions.explanation: Jim Sardonis carved 'Reverence' in 1989; the 13-foot tails symbolize the fragility of the planet.

questions.q: What oddball roadside attraction towers 38 feet over Flynn Avenue in Burlington's South End?
questions.explanation: Artist Bren Alvarez stacked 38 file drawers in 2002 as 'File Under So. Co., Waiting for...' — a jab at bureaucratic delays on the Southern Connector road project.

questions.q: Burlington High School's athletic teams have what nautically improbable mascot for a landlocked state?
questions.explanation: Burlington High's Seahorses have puzzled and delighted since the 1930s — a nod to the lake.

questions.q: Which Burlington neighborhood's streets — Caroline, Charlotte, Katherine, Margaret — give it the nickname 'Five Sisters'?
questions.explanation: The Five Sisters neighborhood in the South End is named for its cluster of women's-name streets.

questions.q: Burlington's historically working-class immigrant neighborhood, now its most diverse, is known as what?
questions.explanation: The ONE has welcomed waves of French-Canadian, Irish, Italian, and — more recently — refugee families for 150 years.

questions.q: Winooski's historic nickname, a nod to both the Abenaki name and its pungent crop, is what?
questions.explanation: 'Winooski' means wild-onion land in Abenaki, so the city became the Onion City — its minor-league past even featured an onion mascot.

questions.q: Winooski's woolen mills, which powered the city for a century, sat where?
choices: At the falls of the Winooski River
questions.explanation: The Champlain Mill and its neighbors harnessed Winooski Falls; the renovated mill buildings now hold offices and apartments.

questions.q: St. Albans, once headquarters of the Central Vermont Railway, carries what nickname?
questions.explanation: St. Albans grew up around the Central Vermont's shops and yards — and still hosts the Vermont Maple Festival.

questions.q: What covers the dome of the Vermont State House?
questions.explanation: The State House dome is gilded with genuine 23.7-karat gold leaf, re-applied roughly every generation.

questions.q: Barre's Hope Cemetery is famous for what?
choices: Elaborate granite gravestones carved by the quarry city's artisans — including a soccer ball and a race car
questions.explanation: Barre's Italian stonecutters carved their own monuments; Hope Cemetery is an open-air granite sculpture museum.

questions.q: Brookfield, Vermont maintains a beloved bridge across Sunset Lake that does what?
questions.explanation: The Brookfield Floating Bridge, the only one of its kind in Vermont (rebuilt 2015), floats because the lake is too deep for pilings.

questions.q: Rutland's Halloween Parade, running since 1960, has a special place in the history of what?
choices: Comic books — Batman and other DC/Marvel stories were set at it
questions.explanation: Local superfan Tom Fagan befriended comics writers, and 1970s Marvel and DC issues actually depict the Rutland parade — a legendary comics crossover.

questions.q: Ethan Allen's restored 1787 farmhouse stands in which Burlington natural area?
questions.explanation: The Ethan Allen Homestead sits in the Winooski River Intervale, where Allen spent his final years.

questions.q: Burlington's Intervale is best known today as what?
choices: A hub of community farms and gardens in the river floodplain
questions.explanation: The Intervale Center incubates a dozen farms on 340 floodplain acres a mile from downtown — pioneering urban agriculture since 1988.

questions.q: Vermont's Air National Guard, based at BTV, flies which controversial jet over Chittenden County?
questions.explanation: The Green Mountain Boys became the first Guard unit to fly F-35s in 2019, to cheers and noise complaints alike.

questions.q: Vermont's National Guard units proudly carry what historic nickname?
questions.explanation: The Vermont Guard officially uses the Green Mountain Boys name and a version of their 1777 flag.

questions.q: The Green Mountain Boys' 1777 battle flag, still flown across Vermont, looks like what?
choices: A green field with 13 white stars scattered in a blue canton
A white field with a green mountain
A red field with a pine tree
questions.explanation: The green flag with its randomly scattered stars is one of America's oldest surviving battle flag designs.

questions.q: In 1776, Benedict Arnold's makeshift American fleet delayed the British at which Lake Champlain battle?
questions.explanation: Arnold's outgunned gunboats bought a crucial year at Valcour Island in October 1776; the recovered gunboat Philadelphia sits in the Smithsonian.

questions.q: The Lake Champlain Maritime Museum sails a full-size replica of which 1776 gunboat?
questions.explanation: Philadelphia II, built at Basin Harbor, replicates Arnold's gunboat raised from the lake in 1935.

questions.q: Among Lake Champlain's protected shipwrecks is the world's only known intact wreck of what kind of vessel?
questions.explanation: The Burlington Bay horse ferry, powered by horses on a treadmill, is the only known surviving horse-powered boat wreck — part of Vermont's Underwater Historic Preserves.

questions.q: The Spirit of Ethan Allen III offers what on Lake Champlain?
choices: Scenic and dinner cruises from Burlington
Car ferry service to New York
questions.explanation: The 500-passenger cruise boat has run narrated tours from the Burlington waterfront for decades.

questions.q: The Lake Champlain Transportation Company, which ran ferries between Vermont and New York until recently, claimed what superlative?
choices: The longest ferry route in the country
The only steam ferries left in the U.S.
America's oldest continuously operating inland ferry company (since 1826)
questions.explanation: LCT traced its charter to 1826; its Grand Isle–Plattsburgh crossing ran 24/7 for decades.

questions.q: ECHO, the science center and aquarium on Burlington's waterfront, is named for whom?
choices: Senator Patrick Leahy (its full name honors him)
questions.explanation: The ECHO Leahy Center for Lake Champlain honors Patrick and Marcelle Leahy; ECHO stands for Ecology, Culture, History, Opportunity.

questions.q: Amtrak's Ethan Allen Express finally reached Burlington in 2022, connecting the Queen City directly to where?
questions.explanation: After decades of advocacy, the extended Ethan Allen Express now runs from Burlington's Union Station to NYC via Rutland.

questions.q: Amtrak's other Vermont train, running up the Connecticut River valley to St. Albans, is called what?
questions.explanation: The Vermonter replaced the overnight Montrealer in 1995 and serves Brattleboro, Montpelier, and Essex Junction daily.

questions.q: Vermont is one of the few states covered by a single telephone area code. Which one — practically a state emblem?
questions.explanation: '802' is shorthand for Vermont identity, on hats, stickers, and beer cans everywhere.

questions.q: Burlington's alternative weekly, publishing since 1995 and famously still free and locally owned, is called what?
questions.explanation: Seven Days covers Vermont news, arts, and its legendary personals; The Other Paper serves South Burlington.

questions.q: Vermont's dominant TV station, broadcasting Channel 3 from Burlington since 1954, is…
questions.explanation: WCAX, long owned by the Martin family, is Vermont's CBS affiliate and news institution.

questions.q: Burlington's daily newspaper, founded in 1827, is called what?
questions.explanation: The Free Press has published since 1827, though its newsroom is a shadow of its Gannett-era size.

questions.q: Vermont's largest hospital, atop Burlington's hill, was renamed what in 2014?
choices: The University of Vermont Medical Center
questions.explanation: Fletcher Allen Health Care became the UVM Medical Center; the network is Vermont's largest private employer.

questions.q: For years Burlingtonians called the stalled downtown redevelopment site at the old mall simply…
questions.explanation: The demolished Burlington Town Center left a giant excavation — 'the pit' — for years before CityPlace construction finally resumed.

questions.q: What's a 'flatlander' in Vermont parlance?
questions.explanation: Flatlanders come from away; 'woodchucks' are born-and-bred rural Vermonters. Both terms are wielded with affection. Mostly.

questions.q: Complete the classic Vermont exclamation: 'Jeezum ____!'
questions.explanation: 'Jeezum Crow' is the Vermont-approved way to swear without swearing.

questions.q: Vermont license plates are famously what color?
questions.explanation: The green Vermont plate has been standard for generations — conservation plates aside.

questions.q: Emily's Bridge in Stowe is famous as Vermont's most…
questions.explanation: Legend says jilted Emily haunts the 1844 Gold Brook covered bridge, scratching cars that dawdle after dark.

questions.q: Vermont has more of what per square mile than any other state?
questions.explanation: With over 100 surviving covered bridges, Vermont has the nation's highest density of them.

questions.q: The Cornish–Windsor Bridge, the longest wooden covered bridge in the U.S., connects Windsor, Vermont to Cornish in which state?
questions.explanation: The 449-foot bridge spans the Connecticut River — and because NH owns the river, nearly all of it is technically in New Hampshire.

questions.q: Before settling on 'Vermont,' the independent republic briefly declared itself under what name in 1777?
questions.explanation: For about six months in 1777 the new republic called itself New Connecticut, until Dr. Thomas Young suggested 'Vermont.'

questions.q: The town of Alburgh has an unusual geographic distinction: it occupies…
choices: A peninsula reachable by land only through Canada (or by bridge)
questions.explanation: Alburgh sits on the Alburgh Tongue jutting south from Quebec; without its bridges you'd have to drive through Canada to reach the rest of Vermont.

questions.q: The Sunset Drive-In, one of Vermont's last drive-in theaters, still shows movies in which town north of Burlington?
questions.explanation: The 1948 Sunset Drive-In on Porters Point Road in Colchester runs four screens all summer.

questions.q: UVM maintains the historic Morgan Horse Farm, breeding the state animal, in which town near Middlebury?
questions.explanation: The UVM Morgan Horse Farm in Weybridge has bred Morgans since the 1870s, continuing Colonel Battell's line.

questions.q: Salmon Hole, a storied Burlington-Winooski fishing spot, lies directly below what?
choices: The Winooski One dam at Winooski Falls
questions.explanation: Salmon Hole's pool below Winooski Falls draws anglers for landlocked salmon, steelhead, and enormous carp stories.

questions.q: Fort Montgomery, the massive 1840s fortification at the north end of Lake Champlain, is nicknamed 'Fort Blunder' because…
choices: Its first version was accidentally built on the Canadian side of the border
Its cannons faced the wrong way
questions.explanation: Surveyors goofed: the original 1818 fort went up north of the 45th parallel in Canada; the border was later adjusted by treaty and a new fort built.

questions.q: Burlington's First Night celebration, one of the country's longest-running, happens when?
questions.explanation: First Night Burlington (now 'Highlight') has filled downtown venues with performances every December 31 since 1983.

questions.q: Which brewery threw Burlington's raucous Mardi Gras parade from 1996 until the tradition ended in the 2010s?
questions.explanation: Magic Hat's Mardi Gras parade brought floats and beads to a snowy Church Street for two decades, raising money for local nonprofits.
